reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review context, full TestScript StructureDefinition report, deterministic aggregate, direct behavior findings for TestScript, and shared Resource/DomainResource behavior context. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior was treated as context only because the assigned artifact is TestScript, not Resource or DomainResource.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 TestScript is trial-use/FMM 2, so the compatibility burden is neutral rather than normative. That softens expectations for retaining a specialized testing resource, but it does not erase migration impact for conformance, certification, regression-testing, and implementation-quality workflows that adopted TestScript.

overall.oneLineConclusion: TestScript is absent from R6 core, so R4 TestScript assets need a resource-level retirement, relocation, or compatibility-model migration rather than ordinary element-by-element conversion.

reasoning.thesisMd: The controlling fact is resource identity loss: R6 core has no `StructureDefinition-TestScript`, no package-index TestScript entry, and no obvious in-core successor preserving the R4 executable test-script model. A migration program is already unavoidable for any system that stores, validates, executes, searches, or advertises TestScript.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: This is not a moderate local remodel. R4 TestScript's canonical resource shell plus executable origin/destination, metadata, fixtures, variables, setup/test/teardown operations, and assertions have no same-resource R6 landing place. Adjacent R6 resources may capture documentation, scenarios, requirements, or capabilities, but they do not provide a direct executable TestScript successor; migration is therefore inventory/triage plus possible R4 compatibility retention or external-package mapping.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because the whole resource type disappears, preserving individual child paths has low independent leverage unless the standards decision is to preserve a deprecated/retired TestScript shell or publish an official compatibility package. That does lower the value of piecemeal element preservation, but it does not mean the break is harmless: resource identity, endpoint/search discoverability, and explicit successor guidance remain high-value compatibility levers.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The main less-breaking base design would be retaining `TestScript` in R6 core as retired/deprecated, possibly with the R4 element tree and terminology intact and strong guidance to move future work elsewhere. That would materially help old instances, SDKs, validators, endpoints, and search parameters, but it has real standards cost: continued stewardship of a specialized FMM 2 executable testing grammar. For the child content model and local invariants, less-breaking alternatives are mostly dependent on that same top-level retention decision rather than separate low-cost local fixes.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The two direct behavior findings reinforce the same resource-removal migration: R6 base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises a TestScript REST endpoint, and TestScript-specific search surfaces disappear because the base resource is gone. They matter for repositories, SDKs, and conformance tooling, but they are derivative of the resource lifecycle decision. The eleven shared Resource/DomainResource findings are real cross-resource context but are not scored as TestScript-specific because TestScript is not the assigned Resource or DomainResource artifact.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate's major migration `Yes`, shape `removed-or-replaced-resource`, and `migration-program-dominates` posture. The important nuance is that this posture should not be read as dismissing the two `Revisit` structure findings: it means the standards review should focus on whether to retain or replace the resource identity and compatibility surfaces, not on isolated child-path preservation.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high that TestScript is absent from the supplied R6 core package. Confidence is lower about HL7's intended rationale or successor because official ballot notes, rendered narrative, external IGs, and live terminology history were outside the supplied local package evidence.

findingConsiderations.title: TestScript is absent from the R6 core package
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the resource-level break. Any R4 instance with `resourceType: "TestScript"` lacks an R6 core resource definition, generated model, canonical StructureDefinition, endpoint, or search surface. It makes a migration program unavoidable and remains the main standards-review question: retire/remove outright, relocate, or preserve a deprecated compatibility shell.

findingConsiderations.title: The R4 executable test content model has no R6 core structural landing place
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This finding explains why the break is not just a missing resource name. The central executable model--fixtures, variables, setup/test/teardown actions, operations, and assertions--has no direct R6 core target, so migration requires policy and tooling decisions rather than a mechanical field rename.

findingConsiderations.title: TestScript-specific invariants and required bindings no longer have an R6 core enforcement surface
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The loss of `tst-*` invariants and TestScript-specific bindings matters for any legacy compatibility runner, but it is derivative of the resource removal. A strict R6 validator rejects TestScript before reaching these rules, so this is a local migration chore unless standards choose to retain a legacy TestScript definition.

findingConsiderations.title: The full base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource REST endpoints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: For TestScript this means generic clients and conformance tools should not discover a core R6 `/TestScript` REST surface. The break is real for endpoint inventory and SDK generation, but it follows from the resource lifecycle decision rather than adding an independent migration program.

findingConsiderations.title: Search parameters whose only R4 bases were removed resources disappear from the R6 search surface
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: R4 TestScript repositories that searched by TestScript-specific parameters need query and index migration. This reinforces the need for endpoint/search transition guidance, but preserving old search parameters only makes sense if a legacy TestScript endpoint or compatibility package is also preserved.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a high-impact shared Resource behavior finding, but under the review rules it is context only for TestScript because the assigned resource is not Resource or DomainResource. It may still matter to a broader cross-resource migration plan, especially if legacy TestScript is preserved as a non-core artifact.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Shared search-parameter metadata changes can affect generic search clients, but they are not TestScript-specific and should not drive the resource-level conclusion for a removed resource.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Confirm the official R6 disposition for TestScript. If it moved to an external IG or tooling package, cite that successor and migration path; if it was retired without successor, publish explicit retirement guidance.

For implementers, inventory stored and executable TestScript assets and retain the R4 TestScript StructureDefinition, related terminology, and validator/test-runner logic for any legacy compatibility path.

Standards review should decide whether a retired/deprecated TestScript shell or official compatibility package is worth carrying to preserve canonical resolution, generated APIs, validation, endpoint metadata, and search metadata for one transition cycle.

If legacy REST/search compatibility is desired, document implementation-specific `/TestScript` endpoint support and map the R4 TestScript search parameters explicitly rather than relying on R6 core artifacts.

caveats: Only the supplied local R4/R6 core packages and reports were reviewed; external IG packages or rendered ballot pages may identify an official successor.
Live terminology and THO history for TestScript operation/assertion code systems were not checked.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered only as context under the review rules.
